question.text: A valid Will has to be written and signed by the testator in the presence of how many witnesses?

explanation.text: The Logic: For a Will to be valid, it must be written and signed by the testator in the presence of two witnesses, who in turn attest the Will by signing it. The witnessing requirement establishes that the testator signed the document voluntarily and was competent at the time of execution. Registration of the Will is permitted but is not mandatory. The Trap: "One witness" understates the legal requirement and would render the Will procedurally defective on attestation grounds. "Three witnesses" and "four witnesses" exceed the prescribed minimum; while extra witnesses do not invalidate the Will, the law specifically requires two. Note: The two-witness requirement and the optional (non-mandatory) nature of Will registration are stated in the cited NISM Series XVII Retirement Adviser workbook discussion of Wills. The framing above is presented as general estate-planning knowledge consistent with those criteria, and does not rely on any claim that registration provides stronger evidence of authenticity.
